songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Portland set with a soaring Dark Star > Eyes Of The World > China Doll
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert builds to an exceptional Dark Star → Eyes Of The World → China Doll sequence that showcases Jerry’s soaring leads and Phil’s percolating bass. The second‑set maintains high energy with tight interplay from Keith and solid drumming, while the first set delivers solid renditions of classics like Mexicali Blues and Box of Rain.
ai_show_review.review: Portland’s June 24‑1973 show finds the Dead in top form, delivering a blistering second set anchored by a spectacular Dark Star → Eyes Of The World → China Doll medley. Jerry’s guitar soars throughout, especially during the extended improvisations, while Phil’s bass provides a jazzy, driving undercurrent that propels the jams forward. Keith adds tasteful piano textures near the climax of the Dark Star, and Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming—though a bit recessed early on—locks in tightly once the mix clears. The first set may be uneven, but it still offers highlights like Mexicali Blues, Box of Rain, and a rare ’73 version of Bertha that adds historical flavor. Overall, the show radiates high energy from start to finish, making it a must‑listen for fans of this era.

best_recording.reason: Complete show with solid soundboard quality, capturing the full Dark Star medley and overall high‑energy performance.

key_highlights: Exceptional Dark Star → Eyes Of The World → China Doll medley with soaring guitar and tight rhythm section.
Strong second‑set energy culminating in high‑octane jams.
Rare ’73 version of Bertha adds a special treat.
Soundboard recording captures the performance clearly despite early mix issues.

band_performance.Jerry: Soaring guitar work shines, especially during the Dark Star → Eyes → China Doll sequence; his playing is described as special and consistently strong throughout.
band_performance.Phil: Percolating bass rhythms drive the improvisations, with a memorable jazzy vamp that pulls listeners in; noted for a “Philo‑stop” vibe that anchors the jams.
band_performance.Bob: Solid rhythm guitar and vocal contributions, with phased effects adding texture on several numbers.
band_performance.Keith: Tasteful piano touches enhance the Dark Star jam and are called amazing on tracks like Mexicali Blues and China Cat Sunflower.
band_performance.Billy: Drumming is brilliant and underpins the improvisations; early kit balance is a bit low but improves as the show progresses.
